s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain with anemia and hemodynamic stability in a patient with a history of hypervascular liver lesions
salient_findings: Anemia with a hemoglobin level of 4.4 mmol/L
Subcapsular hepatic bleeding on abdominal ultrasound
Active bleeding from a hypervascular lesion in segment IV on contrast-enhanced CT
key_facts: 64-year-old white man
Admitted in March 2016
On therapeutic anticoagulation for paroxysmal pre-shimmering
History of two hypervascular liver lesions in segment IV
Biopsies in August 2015 showed histologically proven adenoma without malignancy
Hemodynamically stable on presentation
No weight loss, fever, or constitutional symptoms
Normal α-fetoprotein, carcinoembryonic antigen, and carbohydrate antigen 19-9 levels
Abdominal ultrasound revealed subcapsular hepatic bleeding
Contrast-enhanced CT confirmed active bleeding from one of the two hypervascular lesions
Angiographic embolization and conservative management resolved bleeding

shortlist.label: Hepatocellular adenoma with rupture
shortlist.why_kept: History of hypervascular liver lesions with biopsy-proven adenoma and evidence of rupture

shortlist.label: Hepatocellular carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Suspicion for atypical hepatocellular carcinoma due to persistent hypervascular lesions and central necrosis

shortlist.label: Focal nodular hyperplasia with hemorrhage
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of acute abdominal pain and anemia in a patient with hypervascular liver lesions

shortlist.label: Hemangioma with rupture
shortlist.why_kept: Common benign liver lesion that can cause rupture and bleeding

shortlist.label: Intrahepatic arteriovenous malformation with rupture
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of acute abdominal pain and anemia due to rupture of a vascular malformation

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of histologically proven adenoma without malignancy, and the presentation of acute-onset abdominal pain and anemia with evidence of subcapsular hepatic bleeding and active bleeding from one of the hypervascular lesions is consistent with rupture of a hepatocellular adenoma.

rejected.label: Hepatocellular carcinoma
rejected.why: Normal tumor markers and no typical features of hepatocellular carcinoma on imaging

rejected.label: Focal nodular hyperplasia with hemorrhage
rejected.why: No characteristic central scar on imaging and histological diagnosis of adenoma in the past

rejected.label: Hemangioma with rupture
rejected.why: Hemangiomas are typically not hypervascular on CT and have a different appearance on MRI

rejected.label: Intrahepatic arteriovenous malformation with rupture
rejected.why: No evidence of an arteriovenous malformation on imaging and the lesions were described as hypervascular adenomas in the past
